links.quote: Rubber means the sum of the materials (for example, natural rubber, synthetic rubber, carbon black, oils, sulfur) that are combined in specific formulations

aiCheck.note: The quote defines rubber as a combination of materials including natural rubber, which describes the compounding process.

links.quote: Compounded rubber, unvulcanized, in primary forms or in plates, sheets or strip… Other forms… of unvulcanized rubber

aiCheck.note: The HS nomenclature headings show that unvulcanised rubber in other forms is made from compounded unvulcanised rubber.
The quote explicitly states that 'camel-back' strips (an unvulcanised rubber form) are used for retreading rubber tires.

links.quote: The term “natural rubber latex” means rubber that is produced by the natural rubber latex process… Products are formed from natural rubber latex by dipping, extruding, or coating.

aiCheck.note: The quote states that products are formed from natural rubber latex by extrusion, which is the process used to make vulcanised rubber thread.

links.quote: the expression “rubber” means the following products, whether or not vulcanised or hard : natural rubber, balata, gutta-percha, guayule, chicle and similar natural gums

aiCheck.note: The WCO note states that 'rubber' includes natural rubber whether or not hard, supporting that hard rubber is made from natural rubber.

links.quote: The term “raw material” shall mean all natural and synthetic rubber, carbon black, oils, chemical compounds, and fabric used in the manufacture of general molded, extruded, and fabricated rubber products.

aiCheck.note: The cited regulation confirms that natural rubber is a raw material used to manufacture general molded, extruded, and fabricated rubber products, which encompasses vulcanised rubber shapes.

links.quote: Products are formed from dry natural rubber by compression molding, extrusion, or by converting the sheets into a solution for dipping.

aiCheck.note: The FDA regulation states that products are formed from dry natural rubber by converting sheets into a solution for dipping, which is the process used to make vulcanised rubber apparel such as gloves.
